stem: Which factor best explains why dietary advice alone may be hard for some families in a remote Aboriginal community to follow?

options.text: Healthy food may cost up to 30% more in rural areas, and welfare recipients may need about 50% of disposable income to achieve a healthy diet
Higher health funding per person means food access is no longer a practical issue
Iron deficiency in this setting is usually due to a single cause rather than multiple factors
Iron deficiency is uncommon in remote settings, so prevention counselling is usually unnecessary
Iron deficiency mainly affects hearing and is not linked to cognition

explanation: Healthy food affordability is the key issue. Healthy food may cost up to 30% more in rural areas, and welfare recipients may need about 50% of disposable income to achieve a healthy diet, so dietary advice alone may be difficult to implement.

rationale: Iron deficiency in Aboriginal children in remote settings is multifactorial, and food affordability can limit the practicality of dietary prevention advice.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because healthy food can be substantially more expensive in rural areas, and the proportion of income needed to buy a healthy diet may be very high for welfare recipients.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because increased health funding per person does not remove the practical barrier of food cost and access.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because iron deficiency in this setting is multifactorial, not usually due to a single cause.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because iron deficiency is common in remote settings, so prevention counselling remains important.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because iron deficiency is linked with adverse health and cognitive outcomes, not mainly hearing effects.
